The overall scenario is intended to illustrate passive information gathering.

questions.prompt: Which two basic metrics should be taken into consideration when assessing a severity to a vulnerability during an assessment? (choose 2)

options.text: The age of the hardware running the software that contains the vulnerability
The likelihood that an adversary can and will exploit the vulnerability
The time involved in choosing replacement software to replace older systems
The impacts that an exploit of the vulnerability will have on the organization

questions.explanation: Likelihood and organizational impact are core risk-assessment considerations. They inform prioritization alongside technical severity and exposure; hardware age or replacement effort alone does not establish how serious a weakness is.

questions.prompt: You need to manage security risks at your company. In which order should you complete the actions?
questions.answerLabel: A then B then C then D
questions.explanation: First identify risks, then evaluate and prioritize them, implement appropriate treatment, and monitor the result. Monitoring can reveal changing conditions that require another assessment, so risk management is iterative.

questions.prompt: Your manager asks you to review the output of some vulnerability scans and report anything that may require escalation. Which two findings should you report for further investigation as potential security vulnerabilities? (Choose 2.)
questions.explanation: A disabled firewall and unexpected open ports merit investigation. An open port is not automatically a vulnerability: establish whether the service is necessary, authorized, patched, and exposed appropriately before escalating its risk.

questions.prompt: You notice that a new CVE has been shared to an email group that you belong to. What should you do first with the CVE?

options.text: Record the CVE as part of the disaster recovery plan.
Research measures to prevent the CVE from attacking the network.
Add the CVE to the firewall rules for your organization.
Look up details of the vulnerability to determine whether it applies to your network

questions.explanation: A CVE identifier refers to a documented vulnerability. First compare affected products, versions, and conditions with your inventory; only then choose relevant mitigation. The CVE itself is not malware that can be blocked as a firewall rule.

questions.prompt: Your supervisor suspects that someone is attempting to gain access to a Windows computer by guessing user account IDs and passwords. The supervisor asks you to use the Windows Event Viewer security logs to verify the attempts. Which two audit policy events provide information to determine whether someone is using invalid credentials to attempt to log in to the computer? (Choose 2.)
questions.explanation: Failed logon or credential-validation events and account-lockout evidence help identify password guessing. The phrase Account lockout success is best interpreted as a successful audit record of a lockout, such as event 4740, not a successful user login. Inspect failed logon event 4625 and its details; an object-access failure alone does not establish invalid login credentials.

questions.prompt: Your supervisor tells you that you will participate in a CVSS assessment. What will you be doing?

options.text: Performing penetration tests on internal network devices and end system
Interviewing users to determine their level of cybersecurity awareness
Evaluating end system security and scoring software vulnerabilities
Analyzing host logs to identify abnormal activities

questions.explanation: CVSS provides a standardized way to describe and score vulnerability severity. It does not perform a penetration test or measure awareness, and its score is an input to risk prioritization rather than a complete organizational risk assessment.

questions.prompt: While conducting a risk evaluation at your company, you identify risks that are related to the web server located in the office. The risks include hardware and software failure as well as web service interruption caused by cyber attacks. You recommend purchasing insurance and hiring another organization to maintain the web server to help mitigate the risks.
questions.explanation: Insurance transfers some financial consequences to an insurer. Outsourcing can share or transfer responsibilities, but the organization retains accountability and residual risk; transfer does not remove the underlying threat.

questions.prompt: You are working with the senior administration team to identify potential risks. Which phase of risk management are you in?
questions.explanation: Identifying relevant threats, assets, and exposures contributes to building a risk profile. Selecting treatments and measuring residual risk follow assessment; the source's named phase is broad rather than a universal standard label.

questions.prompt: Move each cybersecurity tool from the list on the left to the correct location on the Vulnerability Management Process diagram on the right

pairs.right: Nmap; Nessus Scanner
CVSS
Windows Auto Update; Patch Management Software

questions.explanation: Nmap helps discover hosts and services, Nessus scans for vulnerabilities, CVSS supports severity prioritization, and update or patch tools remediate weaknesses. CVSS is a scoring system rather than a scanner, and business context must supplement it.

questions.prompt: Your organization's SIEM system alerts you that users are connecting to an unusual URL. You need to determine whether the URL is malicious and what type of threat it represents. What should you do?

options.text: Submit the URL to a threat intelligence portal for analysis
Ask users why they visited the website.
Visit the URL to determine whether the websites is legitimate
Block the URL by placing it on the network block list.

questions.explanation: A trusted threat-intelligence service can help analyze a suspicious URL without visiting it directly from a normal workstation. Avoid submitting URLs containing secrets or sensitive internal data to public services; use approved internal analysis when appropriate.

questions.prompt: Move each cybersecurity term from the list on the left to the correct description on the right.

pairs.right: People, property, or data
An action that causes a negative impact
The potential for loss, damage, or destruction
A weakness that potentially exposes Organizations to cyber attacks

questions.explanation: These are the intended matches for asset, threat, risk, and vulnerability. More precisely, a threat is a potential cause of harm rather than only an action that already caused damage. Risk assessment also considers likelihood and impact; a vulnerability is the exploitable weakness.

questions.prompt: Which activity is an example of active reconnaissance performed during a penetration test?

options.text: Using a browser to view the HTTP source code of company webpages
Gathering employee information from available web directories and social media
Performing an Nmap port scan on the LAN to determine types of connected devices and open ports
Searching the WHOIS database for the owner and technical contact information for a domain.

questions.explanation: An Nmap port scan sends probes to target systems, making it active reconnaissance. WHOIS and social- media research use public information; directly retrieving a target web page also makes contact, so source context matters.

questions.prompt: Which two basic metrics should be taken into consideration when assigning a severity to a vulnerability during an assessment? (Choose 2)

options.text: The likelihood that an adversary can and will exploit the vulnerability
The impacts that an exploit of the vulnerability will have on the organization
The time involved n choosing replacement software to replace older systems
The age of the hardware running the software that contains the vulnerability

questions.explanation: Likelihood of exploitation and organizational impact guide risk prioritization. Technical severity, exposure, and asset importance also matter; hardware age and replacement planning alone cannot determine the risk posed by the weakness.

questions.prompt: What are two disadvantages of public vulnerability databases? (choose 2)

options.text: Threat actors can access the databases to learn how to vary their threats to avoid detection.
Publicly available database are incompatible with most security platform
It can take a long time for reported vulnerabilities to be investigated and approved for addition to the databases
It is costly for intelligence analysts to document and submit newly discovered vulnerabilities.

questions.explanation: Public vulnerability details can help adversaries plan attacks or adapt techniques, while investigation and publication delays can leave databases incomplete. These are the intended trade-offs in A and C. Public databases also provide major defensive value; public access does not automatically defeat detection, and platform incompatibility is not universal.

questions.prompt: Which command displays both the configured DNS server information and the IP address resolution for a URL?
questions.explanation: nslookup displays the DNS server used and DNS record results for a queried name. A hostname is queried rather than an entire URL containing a scheme or path. ping and traceroute perform different reachability and route diagnostics.

questions.prompt: Your manager asks you to review the output of some vulnerability scans and report anything that might require escalation. Which two findings should you report for further investigation as potential security vulnerabilities? (Choose 2.)

options.text: DNS packets with common domain names

questions.explanation: Missing application patches expose systems to known, exploitable vulnerabilities (CVEs), and unexpected open ports expand the network attack surface. Routine SSH traffic and standard DNS queries for common domain names represent normal network activity rather than vulnerability scan findings.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is true regarding the incident response process?

options.text: It is a reactive process that is only initiated after an incident has occurred.
It is a proactive process that focuses on preventing incidents from occurring.
It is an iterative process that involves continuous improvement based on lessons learned.
It is a one-time process that is only performed when an organization first establishes its security program.

questions.explanation: Incident response includes preparation, detection, response, recovery, and improvement. Lessons from incidents should improve controls and procedures, so it is a continuing activity rather than a one-time response.

questions.prompt: You need a software solution that performs the following tasks. ◦ Compiles network data ◦ Logs information from many sources ◦ Provides orchestration in the form of case management ◦ Automates incident response workflows What product should you use?
questions.explanation: SOAR emphasizes orchestration, case management, and automated response playbooks. SIEM emphasizes collecting and correlating security events; modern platforms may combine capabilities, but the workflow-automation requirement makes SOAR the best fit.

questions.prompt: Move each worm mitigation step from the list on the left to the correct description on the right.

pairs.right: Contain the spread of the worm into your network and within your network. Compartmentalize uninfected parts of your network.
Start patching all systems and, if possible, scanning for vulnerable systems.
Track down each infected machine in your network. Disconnect, remove, or block infected machines from the network.
Clean and patch each infected system. Some worms may require complete core system reinstallations to clean the system.

questions.explanation: Containment limits spread; inoculation patches uninfected targets; quarantine isolates infected systems; treatment removes infection and restores trusted operation. These activities may overlap in real incidents rather than following a rigid one-time sequence.

questions.prompt: You are reviewing your company's disaster recovery plan. Which two daily data backup actions should the plan include? (Choose 2.)

options.text: Back up the data by using RAID on a local external hard drive with a secondary power source.
Back up the data to removable media and store it off-site.
Back up the data by using cloud services.
Back up each department's data to a separate local server.

questions.explanation: Off-site removable-media backups and appropriately secured cloud backups can retain recovery copies away from local disasters. RAID is redundancy, not a backup: it does not inherently protect against deletion, ransomware, or site loss. Separate local copies may help recovery but lack the off-site protection of B and C.

questions.prompt: Move each NIST Incident Response Lifecycle phase from the list on the left to the correct description on the right.

pairs.right: Mitigates the impact of the incident
Evaluates incident indicators to determine whether they are legitimate attacks and alerts the organization of the incidents.
Reports the cause and cost of the incident and the steps to prevent future incidents.
Establishes an incident response capability to ensure that organizational assets are sufficiently secure.

questions.explanation: The four labels are the historical NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2 lifecycle. Preserve them for older course material, but Rev. 3, published in 2025, aligns incident response with CSF 2.0 and supersedes Rev. 2.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of a disaster recovery plan as compared to a business continuity plan?

options.text: Allowing staff to continue to serve customers throughout a disaster
Keeping the business open in some capacity during a disaster
Restoring data access and an IT infrastructure as quickly as possible

questions.explanation: Disaster recovery focuses on restoring IT systems and data after disruption. Business continuity covers maintaining critical business operations more broadly, potentially through alternate people, facilities, or manual procedures.

questions.prompt: For each statement, select True if it is a common motivation to commit cyber attacks or False if is not.

pairs.left: A person becomes disgruntled at work.
pairs.right: TRUE

pairs.left: A person wants to protect personal data.
pairs.right: FALSE

pairs.left: A person wants to advance a social agenda.
pairs.right: TRUE

questions.explanation: Disgruntlement and ideological goals are recognized attacker motivations. Protecting one's own data through authorized defensive action is not itself a motive for an unauthorized attack. Motivation never establishes authorization to test another system.

questions.prompt: Move each NIST incident Response Lifecycle phase from the list on the left to the correct description on the right.

pairs.right: Mitigate the impact of the incident.
Report the cause and cost of the incident And the steps to prevent future incident
Evaluates incident indicators to determine whether they are legitimate attacks and alerts the organization of the incidents.
Establishes an incident response capability to Ensure that organizational assets are Sufficiently secure.

questions.explanation: Preparation establishes readiness; detection and analysis identifies and validates incidents; containment, eradication, and recovery limits harm and restores service; post-incident work captures lessons. These are Rev. 2 historical labels.

questions.prompt: You are monitoring the syslog server and observe that the DNS server is sending messages with a Warning severity. What do these messages indicate about the operation of the DNS server?

options.text: The DNS server is unusable due to a severe malfunction and is shutting down
The server has a hardware error that does not require immediate attention
A condition exists that will cause errors in the future if the issue is not fixed.
An error condition is occurring that must be addressed immediately

questions.explanation: Syslog Warning has severity 4 and indicates a condition requiring attention before it becomes more serious. C is the closest supplied choice, but a warning does not guarantee future errors. Error is severity 3 and Emergency is severity 0.

questions.prompt: Move each worm mitigation step from the list on the left to the correct description on the right.

pairs.right: Clean and patch infected system
Remove or block infected system From the network
Patch uninfected systems to deprive The worm of more available targets
Compartmentalize and segment the Network to limit the spread of the Worm to areas already infected

questions.explanation: Quarantine removes or blocks infected hosts; containment limits spread through segmentation; inoculation patches uninfected systems; treatment cleans and restores affected systems.

questions.prompt: Move the appropriate control measures from the list on the left to the correct descriptions on the right. You may use each control measure once, more than once or not at all. Note. You will receive partial for each correct answer.

pairs.right: Discover unwanted event
Avert the occurrence of an event
Restore a system after an event

questions.explanation: Preventive controls aim to stop an event, detective controls identify it, and corrective controls restore or improve the affected system afterward. A control can serve more than one purpose depending on its implementation.

questions.prompt: What are two natural disasters that would cause a company to implement a disaster recovery plan? (choose 2).
questions.explanation: Floods and volcanic eruptions are natural hazards. Hazardous-material spills and nuclear contamination are normally treated as technological or human-caused hazards in this classification, though disasters can have cascading causes.

questions.prompt: You are a security analyst. You are reviewing output from the SIEM. You notice an alert concerning malicious files detected by the IDS. After reviewing the user, device and posture information you determine that it is a valid What should you do next?

options.text: Log the alert and watch for a second occurrence
Prepare notes to present at the weekly cybersecurity team meeting
Update the documentation to include the new alert information

questions.explanation: After validating a credible malicious-file alert, follow the response plan and promptly escalate to the authorized incident-response team. Delaying until a weekly meeting or waiting for another occurrence can allow further compromise.
